headline: Sensex drops 500 points as U.S. Fed rate-hike fears and global market weakness trigger profit booking

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: U.S. Fed minutes revived rate-hike fears, highlighting policymakers' focus on inflation risks.
Profit booking emerged after domestic equity markets snapped a two-day rally.
Losses in metals, consumer durables, and IT indices dragged down major benchmark indices.
Weak global cues, including Wall Street slumps and tumbling commodity prices, dented sentiment.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped around 500 points, while Nifty settled below the 25,250 mark.
Titan sank over 4%, pulling down the consumer durables and retail segments.
Wall Street benchmark Dow Jones slump over 500 points following Fed minutes publication.
Brent crude slipped below $92 per barrel amid deepening supply glut concerns.
summary: Indian benchmark indices snapped a two-day rally as Sensex tumbled 500 points and Nifty slipped below 25,250 amid profit booking. Renewed fears of U.S. Fed rate hikes severely impacted global market sentiment, causing Wall Street and Asian markets to decline. Heavy sell-offs in consumer durables, metals, and IT stocks led the domestic market decline, with Titan and Bajaj Finance dragging the indices down.
